comment: Semantic-lore probe fixture: dictionary entries plus actions labeled with which entries SHOULD activate by meaning. Positive actions are paraphrases sharing no keyword with their entry (the probe asserts this); negative actions relate to nothing in the set. Precision/recall are swept across thresholds to tune SEMANTIC_LORE_THRESHOLD. Entries follow the trade-coast world of semantic-band-cases.json. Several entries are deliberate near-neighbors (beacon/wreckers/shrine, causeway/pass/ferry, guild/charter/coin) so a threshold that is too loose is punished by a measurable false fire rather than going unnoticed, and the negatives include in-world actions that must still match nothing.

entries.name: The Old Beacon
entries.value: The abandoned lighthouse on the headland above the harbor. Fishermen swear its dead lamp still glows on drowning nights and will not moor beneath it.

entries.name: Marsh Causeway
entries.value: The raised stone road through the tidal marsh, the only route north while the pass is blocked. Sinking stones and toll keepers; locals cross only at low water.

entries.name: Salt Factors' Guild
entries.value: The merchant brotherhood that sets prices in every harbor. Crossing them means no stall, no ferry passage, and cargo that mysteriously spoils.

entries.name: Weck
entries.value: A scarred drover with a long memory for debts. Works the harbor cattle yards; his word is good and his grudges are permanent.

entries.name: The Black Tide
entries.value: A poisonous algal bloom that closes the fisheries some autumns. Fish caught during it sicken whole villages; harbormasters burn tainted catches on the shingle.

entries.name: Trader's Ledger Law
entries.value: Coast custom: a dead trader's ledger binds their heir to every open debt and delivery in it. Refusing the book means refusing the route and its protections.

entries.name: Harrowgate
entries.value: The fortified hill town inland where the mule tracks meet. Its market terrace is the only legal exchange for northbound goods.

entries.name: Sedge Ferry
entries.value: The rope-ferry crossing at the coast road's end, run by the ferrywoman Maren. The only way over the sedge channel with a loaded animal.

entries.name: Harbormaster Sella
entries.value: She assigns every mooring and can impound a hold on suspicion alone. Takes no bribes, remembers every hull that ever slipped its berth owing fees.

entries.name: The Saltpans
entries.value: Shallow evaporation beds south of the harbor where bonded laborers rake the crust into heaps. Debt-work; most who go in do not rake their way out.

entries.name: Wreckers
entries.value: Coastal bands who show lanterns on the cliffs to draw hulls onto the reef, then strip what washes in. Hanged at the tideline when caught.

entries.name: Sedge Fever
entries.value: A wasting marsh sickness that comes with the summer damp. Afflicted villages hang yellow cloth at the road and turn travelers back.

entries.name: Clipped Coin
entries.value: Silver shaved at the rim passes freely inland but not here. Every serious trade on this coast ends with a set of scales on the table.

entries.name: Maren
entries.value: The ferrywoman at the sedge channel. Hauls the rope crossing alone, drinks nothing, and will refuse a passenger she mistrusts without explaining why.

entries.name: Weatherhead Pass
entries.value: The mountain route north, shut by rockfall since spring. Until it clears, everything bound inland goes the long way through the marsh.

entries.name: Night Landings
entries.value: Goods put ashore in the coves after dark to dodge the harbor tithe. Everyone knows which coves; nobody names them to a stranger.

entries.name: Harbor Charter
entries.value: The sealed grant that lets a trading house sell in this port at all. Without one you may buy, but never open a stall or take on freight.

entries.name: Drovers' Company
entries.value: The loose company that runs animals up the mule tracks to the hill market. They set their own departure days and take no cargo they cannot insure.

entries.name: The Equinox Gales
entries.value: Three weeks of autumn storms that shut the harbor mouth entirely. Crews haul boats above the shingle and wait it out drinking.

entries.name: The Drowned Shrine
entries.value: A half-submerged altar below the headland where sailors leave coin before a crossing. Uncovered at low water, gone again by dusk.

actions.name: beacon-paraphrase
actions.text: I climb toward the ruined tower on the headland where no ships anchor.

actions.name: causeway-paraphrase
actions.text: I ask which path through the wetlands is safe for a loaded mule.

actions.name: guild-paraphrase
actions.text: I ask who really decides what a sack of salt sells for around here.

actions.name: tide-paraphrase
actions.text: I ask the fishermen why they are burning their own catch on the beach.

actions.name: ledger-paraphrase
actions.text: I wonder aloud what my father's debts mean for me now that I carry his book.

actions.name: ferry-paraphrase
actions.text: I need to get my animal across the channel at the end of the coast road.

actions.name: harbormaster-paraphrase
actions.text: I ask who has the authority to release a hold that has been impounded.

actions.name: saltpans-paraphrase
actions.text: I watch bonded laborers rake white crust into heaps in the shallow beds.

actions.name: wreckers-paraphrase
actions.text: I hear someone has been showing lanterns on the cliffs to draw hulls onto the reef.

actions.name: fever-paraphrase
actions.text: I ask why that village hangs yellow cloth at the road and turns travelers back.

actions.name: coin-paraphrase
actions.text: I bite the silver I was handed and reach for my scales.

actions.name: maren-paraphrase
actions.text: I look for the woman who hauls the rope crossing alone.

actions.name: pass-paraphrase
actions.text: I ask whether the mountain route north has been cleared of rockfall yet.

actions.name: smuggling-paraphrase
actions.text: I ask about goods that come ashore after dark without meeting a tithe man.

actions.name: charter-paraphrase
actions.text: I ask what sealed grant a trading house needs before it may open a stall.

actions.name: drovers-paraphrase
actions.text: I look for the company that runs animals up the mule tracks to the hill market.

actions.name: gales-paraphrase
actions.text: I ask how many weeks before the autumn storms shut the harbor mouth.

actions.name: shrine-paraphrase
actions.text: I set a coin on the wet altar below the headland before crossing.

actions.name: harrowgate-paraphrase
actions.text: I ask where northbound goods can be legally exchanged inland.

actions.name: weck-paraphrase
actions.text: I ask after the scarred man in the cattle yards who never forgets a debt.

actions.name: neg-smalltalk
actions.text: I trade jokes with a passing shepherd about his dog.

actions.name: neg-camp
actions.text: I water the mule and make camp for the night.

actions.name: neg-mend
actions.text: I sit by the fire and mend the tear in my coat sleeve.

actions.name: neg-weather
actions.text: I study the clouds, wondering if tomorrow brings rain.

actions.name: neg-barnacles
actions.text: I scrape barnacles from the hull while the water is out.

actions.name: neg-lodging
actions.text: I ask the innkeeper for a room with a window over the street.

actions.name: neg-whetstone
actions.text: I sharpen my knife on a whetstone by the door.

actions.name: neg-letter
actions.text: I write a letter home and look for someone heading that way.

actions.name: neg-provisions
actions.text: I buy bread and hard cheese to carry on the road.

actions.name: neg-boots
actions.text: I pull off my boots and pick the grit out of the seams.

actions.name: neg-gulls
actions.text: I watch two gulls fight over something dropped on the stones.

actions.name: neg-sleep
actions.text: I lie awake listening to the rigging knock until I finally sleep.
